name: SOLVE-IT
short_description: Systematic Objective-based Listing of Various Established (Digital) Investigation Techniques, 2025
long_description: This view is the standard categorisation of digital forensic techniques, inspired by the MITTRE ATT&CK cybersecurity resource. This knowledge base is created and described by Chris Hargreaves, Harm van Beek and Eoghan Casey in their paper presented on DFRWS EU 2025 SOLVE-IT: A proposed digital forensics knowledge base inspired by MITTRE ATT&CK. Sciencedirect (FSI).

name: DFRWS
short_description: Standard DFRWS digital forensic investigation model, 2001
long_description: The standard agreed digital forensic investigation workflow at DFRWS 201 USA conference. A Roadmap for Digital Forensic Research, a collective work of all DFRWS attendees.

name: BDFF
short_description: A Standard digital forensic framework, developed by NMa (The Netherlands), 2003
long_description: This framework was created in 2003 by Bart Stout and Jos Griffioen, former employees of The Dutch Competition Authority(NMa), 2003. The motive for this framework was the need for a more robust tailor-made workflow for the big and complex and long-lasting digital forensic (and e-discovery) investigations, which had to be performed. It is a non-linear process, but an iterative process between the different phases. For 15 years, this framework is now a standard in the education program of the Digital Forensic Education programs of the Leiden University of Applied Sciences.

name: CARRIER
long_description: This categorisation of the phases of a digital forensics process, is proposed by Brian Carrier in 2002, in his paper Open Source Digital Forensics Tools. (www.digital-evidence.org)

name: EDRM
long_description: The EDRM is an E-Discovery framework, created by George Socha,Jr and Tom Gelbmann. It gives guidance for the complex e-discovery processes starting with Governance and ending at the Presentation phase, helping to reduce data volumes and increase relevance of the gathered data. EDRM.net. It is a non-linear process, but an iterative process between the different phases.
